description: Diagnose why a fully-qualified Rego query (e.g. "data.authz.allow") produces no value, or falls back to its default. Combines a plain eval, a full-trace eval, and per-condition AST analysis to identify the exact body expression blocking each rule. Handles both runtime failures (trace-based) and indexer elimination (standalone condition eval). A rule written with `default allow := false` always has a value, so `queryResult` reports `default` for it and the same per-rule breakdown follows: the question "why is allow false" is the question this answers. Returns a structured breakdown of which conditions blocked each rule plus a human-readable summary.

input.description: Input document (JSON value) for the query.

inputPath.description: Path to an input JSON file.

paths.description: Policy .rego file paths to load. Mutually exclusive with source.

query.description: Fully-qualified rule reference to explain, e.g. "data.authz.allow". Must match the path you would pass to rego_eval.

source.description: Inline Rego source to analyse. Mutually exclusive with paths.

v0Compatible.description: Read the policy as Rego v0 (`--v0-compatible`), the syntax OPA used before 1.0: rules without `if`, partial sets as `deny[msg] { ... }`. Needed for a policy that has not been migrated, which OPA 1.x otherwise refuses to load. Where the tool also takes a query, the query is read as v0 too, with the future keywords imported so `in`, `every` and `some x in` still work in it.

name: rego_explain_undefined
title: Explain why a Rego query is undefined
